issue.title: ENH: `min_length` kwarg for `simple_cycles`
issue.body:
Just an idea I had while reviewing/thinking about #8111 

`simple_cycles` already has a `length_bound` kwarg to filter out cycles above a certain length. I wonder if it might be possible to add related functionality: i.e. a `minimum_length` keyword to yield cycles that are at least a certain length.

Of course, this could naively be done with a simple filter `[c for c in nx.simple_cycles(G) if len(c) > minimum_length]`, but what I'm interested in is whether there are any *algorithmic* approaches to only finding cycles above a certain length that are of course more efficient than the full cycle-search.

I haven't done any research on this front, but if such approaches exist I think they could be quite valuable!
issue.author: rossbar

comments.body:
This is a really interesting! I can see how a `min_length` parameter built into the algorithm could be much more performant than post-filtering, especially on dense graphs.

Before I dive in, could you point me in the right direction? Are there any specific algorithmic approaches you had in mind when you suggested this? If not, I'd be happy to do some research into efficient ways to modify the existing cycle-finding algorithm to incorporate a minimum length constraint.

Just looking for a bit of guidance for contributing to this. Thanks!
comments.author: krishnaGauss

Nope! Nothing specific in mind - I have not researched this myself, it's just something that I think there are lots of potential use-cases (and I suspect has been studied by others!)

> If not, I'd be happy to do some research into efficient ways to modify the existing cycle-finding algorithm to incorporate a minimum length constraint.

Literature search is definitely the right place to start - this is an (intentionally) open question!
comments.author: rossbar

comments.body:
Hi @rossbar (cc @krishnaGauss),

I tested a minimal change to add a min_length gate inside the bounded-length DFS routine.

Patch under test
```
# original
if w == start:
    yield path[:]
    blen[-1] = 1

elif len(path) < lock.get(w, length_bound):
    path.append(w)
    blen.append(length_bound)
    lock[w] = len(path)
    stack.append(iter(G[w]))
    break

# patch
if w == start and len(path) >= min_length:
    yield path[:]
    blen[-1] = 1

elif w != start and len(path) < lock.get(w, length_bound):
    path.append(w)
    blen.append(length_bound)
    lock[w] = len(path)
    stack.append(iter(G[w]))
    break
```
So when we return to start with len(path) < min_length, we skip both the yield and the blen[-1] = 1 update. The intent is to treat sub-min-length “cycles” as non-cycles and let normal backtracking proceed.

I tested the proposed change with the following cases, and all assertions passed:
```
def test_simple_cycles_min_length_cases(self):
    DG = nx.DiGraph()
    DG.add_edges_from([
        (1, 2), (1, 3), (1, 4),
        (2, 3), (2, 5),
        (3, 4), (3, 6),
        (4, 7),
        (7, 1)
    ])

    assert list(nx.simple_cycles(DG, min_length=3, length_bound=4)) == [[1, 3, 4, 7], [1, 4, 7]]
    assert list(nx.simple_cycles(DG, min_length=4, length_bound=4)) == [[1, 3, 4, 7]]

    G = nx.Graph()
    G.add_edges_from([
        (1, 2), (1, 3), (1, 4),
        (2, 3), (2, 5),
        (3, 4), (3, 6),
        (4, 7),
        (7, 1)
    ])

    assert list(nx.simple_cycles(G, min_length=3, length_bound=4)) == [
        [1, 2, 3], [1, 2, 3, 4], [1, 3, 4], [1, 3, 4, 7], [1, 4, 7]
    ]
    assert list(nx.simple_cycles(G, min_length=4, length_bound=4)) == [
        [1, 2, 3, 4], [1, 3, 4, 7]
    ]

```

Questions for feedback (focused on safety & performance)

1. Correctness: In the relaxation scheme, does skipping blen[-1] = 1 when a too-short cycle is encountered risk breaking any invariants (e.g., missing valid longer cycles, introducing duplicates, or interfering with lock/B propagation)? My current understanding is that this should not cause incorrect results, since we’re only suppressing emission.
2. Performance: Could this choice materially degrade pruning, since we’re not performing the usual relaxation step for sub-min-length hits on start?

Happy to adjust to whichever semantics you think is safer for correctness and less risky for performance. If this direction looks good, I can follow up with tests and docs. Thanks!
comments.author: Aka2210

comments.body:
Hi @rossbar, just checking in on this — I ran a few additional tests locally and the patch seems stable across both directed and undirected graphs.

Would you prefer that I open a PR so it’s easier to review and run CI, or would you rather continue discussion here first?

(Happy to adjust based on your preference!)
comments.author: Aka2210

comments.body:
If `min_length` is added as a free parameter, `simple_cycles` would solve the classic (Karp 1972) NP-complete Hamiltonian Cycle decision problem (`min_length`=n), no hope for efficient algorithms, unless P=NP. Same if `min_length` is close to n up to a constant.
On the other hand, if `min_length` is a small constant, not too many cycles shorter than `min_length` can exist and the suggested filtering is a viable option.
comments.author: FrankBau
